sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, distracted driving, seat belts and child restraints

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A02
Teens with a Level 1 or Level 2 license may not make or take non-emergency calls even hands-free under Kelsey's Law, while Level 3 teens follow the same hands-free rules as adult drivers. [A02]
Why it matters: group phone law; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec05-F19, sec05-F21 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A02
Using GPS is allowed only when you do not type in information by hand, whereas a single tap to start or end a hands-free call is allowed. [A02]
Why it matters: group phone law; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec05-F20, sec05-F21 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A02
The emergency exception lets any driver, teens included, contact police, fire, health-care or other emergency services, but it does not cover ordinary personal calls. [A02]
Why it matters: group phone law; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec05-F17, sec05-F19 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A01
A first hand-held phone offense costs $100, and every later one costs $250. [A01]
Why it matters: group phone law; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec05-F05 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A03
Every passenger under 16 must be buckled in any seat, while for riders 16 and older the handbook's belt rule names only the driver and front-seat passengers. [A03]
Why it matters: group seat belts; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec05-F24 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A03
A child leaves the car seat or booster at age 8 or at 4 feet 9 inches, whichever comes first, though the handbook suggests going by height. [A03]
Why it matters: group child restraints; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec05-F25, sec05-F29 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A03
Children under 4 belong in the rear seat, while a rear-facing seat may sit in front only if the passenger air bag is deactivated. [A03]
Why it matters: group child restraints; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec05-F32, sec05-F33 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A03
Riders under 18 may not ride in an open pickup bed above 15 mph, which is a different age line from the under-16 seat belt rule. [A03]
Why it matters: group child restraints; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec05-F24, sec05-F34 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A03
Air bags add protection but never replace a belt, which belongs across the middle of the chest and low on the hips. [A03]
Why it matters: group seat belts; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec05-F27 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A01
At 65 mph a car covers 24 feet in the quarter second it takes to shift attention, so even tuning a radio carries risk. [A01]
Why it matters: group distraction; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec05-F06, sec05-F07 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0037]
